notes: §1985:VIII.2.4.2 prints the relative ACCESS MODE clause as ACCESS MODE IS with one of three modes, the RELATIVE KEY IS data-name-1 phrase optional after SEQUENTIAL and required after RANDOM or DYNAMIC, and nowhere else. The grammar parses the mode (accessModeClause, accessMode, with MODE and IS optional words) and the key (relativeKeyClause, KEY and IS optional) as two clauses, and the 1985 nesting is restored by VisitRelativeKeyClause, which at 85 refuses with COBOL0900 a RELATIVE KEY that does not directly follow the ACCESS MODE clause (probed: no ACCESS MODE, written before it, separated from it by FILE STATUS, written twice); the SR-12.4.5.2-10 row of Rules refuses RANDOM or DYNAMIC with no key (COBOL0863) and its SR-12.4.5.2-9 row refuses the phrase on a sequential or indexed file. MapAccessMode gives the file its mode. The witness writes and reads three relative files, one per mode, each with the key phrase after its mode, and its output matches.

next.reason: 1985: "ACCESS MODE IS SEQUENTIAL [ RELATIVE KEY IS data-name-1 ] ... RANDOM/DYNAMIC RELATIVE KEY IS data-name-1"; 2023: "[ ORGANIZATION IS ] RELATIVE [ RELATIVE KEY IS data-name-7 ]; ACCESS MODE IS {SEQUENTIAL|RANDOM|DYNAMIC} separate". Key still required for RANDOM/DYNAMIC, but 2023 makes RELATIVE KEY its own clause, so it can be written without any ACCESS MODE clause; 1985 accepted it only inside ACCESS MODE.
